final_message:
I rewrote the `description` in `skills/parquet-schema-check/SKILL.md`. I haven't run any triggering test on the new wording yet.

**Cause:** the old description was `Helps with parquet files.` It names no trigger, so an agent about to call `to_parquet` has no reason to connect that to the skill. The body was fine, so I left it alone.

**New description:**
> Use when about to write a parquet file (to_parquet, write_parquet, pq.write_table, df.write.parquet) for a dataset that has a schema file in schemas/, or when a job reading parquet fails on missing columns, wrong column order, or dtype mismatch.

It starts with "Use when" and names the moment of the write, the common write calls, and the downstream failure symptoms. It doesn't describe the skill's steps, because a description that summarizes the procedure can make agents follow the summary instead of reading the skill.

**Not verified:**
- **Triggering:** I haven't re-run it. The check I'd run is at least three should-load prompts, such as "save this frame to `out/events.parquet`", and three near misses, such as reading a parquet file or writing CSV. I'd run each in a fresh session with the old and new descriptions and compare how many load the skill. Tell me if you want me to set that up.
- **Skill listing:** if descriptions overflow Claude Code's listing budget, it drops whole descriptions, least-used skills first. A skill that is never invoked is a likely candidate to be dropped. If agents still miss it after this change, check `/context` or `/skill-doctor` to see whether this entry is being dropped.

**Left unchanged:** the frontmatter has no `license` field, which the writing-skills checklist requires. No skill in this repo has one, so I didn't add it. If your lint enforces it, tell me which license to use.
